header: THE ALL-INDIA CONSUMER PRICE INDEX FOR INDUSTRIAL WORKERS (AICPI-IW, base 2016 = 100) AND THE DEARNESS ALLOWANCE OF SAIL EMPLOYEES WORKED OUT FROM IT (the CPSE "IDA pattern" of the 2017 pay scales, revised every quarter). THE INDEX comes from the Labour Bureau (Ministry of Labour and Employment, labourbureau.gov.in), which publishes each month's all-India figure on the last day of the next month. I read two of its pages:
* the CPI-IW page, whose chart holds the last twelve months (its script lists the months and the figures);
* the home page, whose box holds the latest two months (so the newest month is there before the chart page is updated).

I merge both. The months must be one after the other, the figures plausible, and the two pages must agree on a month they share. If a page no longer has these things I raise an error and never guess. THE DA (IDA, 2017 pay scales). I worked it out from the orders of the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), read for this:

* OM No. W-02/0028/2017-DPE(WC)-GL-XIII/17 of 3 Aug 2017, para 7: "100% DA neutralization ... DA as on 01.01.2017 will become zero with link point of AICPI 2001=100, which is 277.33 (average of AICPI for the months of September, October & November, 2016) ... The periodicity of adjustment will be once in three months."

* OM F.No. W-02/0039/2017-DPE(WC)-GL-V/20 of 3 Apr 2020: for 1 April 2020 the average of December, January and February is 329.33, the increase over the link point 52, "DA rate 18.7% [52 / 277.33) x 100]". So: IDA % = ( average index of the three months - 277.33 ) / 277.33 x 100, to one decimal place, on the 2001-base index; the quarters are 1 January (September to November), 1 April (December to February), 1 July (March to May) and 1 October (June to August). The Labour Bureau's index is now on base 2016, and it is linked to the 2001 base by the factor 2.88; the orders do not print that factor. Checked against the orders: with the 2016-base figures the formula gives 53.42% for 1 January 2026 (the rate in the DPE order circulated by Coal India: 53.4%) and 59.06% for 1 October 2026 (DPE OM No. W-02/0037/2025-DPE(WC)/FTS-14505 of 27 Oct 2026: 59.1%, which also shows that the figure is rounded to the nearest tenth, not cut). Two further quarters, 54.1% (April 2026, OM of 24 April 2026) and 55.7% (July 2026, OM of 17 July 2026), agree with the orders themselves, which I read on DPE's website on 28 Nov 2026 (scanned pictures, read by eye). See aicpi.selftest.ts. THE ORDERS ARE NOW READ FROM DPE'S SITE EVERY TIME THE RECORD IS LOADED (src/lib/live/dpeOrders.ts): a new order appears on the card by itself; the list below is only the fall-back for the orders that are pictures, whose rates a machine cannot read.

What is NOT established: that SAIL pays exactly this for its employees. It rests on the DPE guidelines SAIL's executives are under, SAIL's agreement of 22 Oct 2021 (reported as giving executives and non-executives the same DA on the same link point) and the figures above; SAIL's own pages could not be read (sail.co.in fails its certificate, the exchange filings refuse access), so SAIL's own circular is the authority. I found nothing that makes SAIL's rule different (no extra factor), and I have invented none.

symbols.name: announcementFor
symbols.sig: export function announcementFor(startsOn: string, orders: DpeOrder[] | undefined): Announcement | null
doc: What the orders say about the quarter that begins on `startsOn`: from DPE's website (the order's PDF, and its rate when the PDF has text) and from my hand list (the rates I read from pictures). A rate read from the site's text wins over my list (it is the later reading of the order itself). Null when neither has an order for the quarter.

behaviours: the chart holds twelve months, Sep 2025 to Aug 2026, with the figures the Labour Bureau shows (147.3 ... 154.4)
the home page box holds the latest two months: Aug 2026 154.4 and Sep 2026 155.5
the two pages are merged into the year to the latest month: 13 months, Sep 2025 to Sep 2026 (the same span as the other one-year charts: the same month a year back to the latest), the latest 155.5
without the home page the twelve months of the chart are still a year of readings, the latest Aug 2026
a home page that cannot be read (no box) leaves the chart as it is
a page without the chart is an error
a chart whose months and figures do not match in number is an error
the two pages must agree on a month they share
a gap in the months is an error
an implausible figure (15.5 for a 155.5) is an error
a record whose latest month is more than three months old is out of date
a record that is shorter than a year is refused

the three months of each quarter: 1 January is September to November, 1 April December to February, 1 July March to May, 1 October June to August (the DPE order of 3 April 2020 uses December to February for 1 April)
1 January 2026: September to November 2025 average 147.73, x 2.88 = 425.47, 53.42% over the link point 277.33, so 53.4%: the rate in the DPE order (circulated by Coal India)

1 October 2026: June to August 2026 average 153.17, x 2.88 = 441.12, increase 163.79, 59.06%, so 59.1%: the rate in DPE's OM of 27 Oct 2026, and it is ROUNDED to the nearest tenth (cut it would be 59.0)
1 April 2026 gives 54.1% and 1 July 2026 gives 55.7%: the rates of the orders themselves (OM of 24 April 2026 and of 17 July 2026, read on DPE's website), so both are in the list of announced rates
the DPE order of 3 April 2020 worked the same way: an average of 329.33 over the link point 277.33 is 52, 18.7% (52 / 277.33 = 18.75%, printed 18.7)
the DPE order of 3 August 2017: the average of September to November 2016 is the link point 277.33, so the DA that day is zero
one point of the index (base 2016) adds 1.04 percentage points of DA (2.88 / 277.33 x 100)
a quarter whose months are not all in the record is not worked out (October 2025 needs June to August 2025)
1 January 2027 is a projection: September 2026 is published (1 of 3), October and November stand at 155.5, so the average is 155.50, x 2.88 = 447.84, 61.48%, 61.5%
a projection with nothing published (a quarter far ahead) is not made, and a quarter fully published is not a projection (known 3)
the quarters of the record on 13 Nov 2026: 1 Jan, 1 Apr, 1 Jul and 1 Oct 2026, then 1 Jan 2027 (projected); 53.4, 54.1, 55.7, 59.1, 61.5
the quarter a date is in: 13 Nov 2026 is in the quarter from 1 October (next 1 January 2027); 1 Jan and 31 Mar are in the first quarter; 1 Apr in the second
the list of announced rates holds the five orders that were read (51.8 from 1 Oct 2025, 53.4, 54.1, 55.7, 59.1 from 1 Oct 2026), in order of date
the formula gives the order's own rate in every quarter of the record that has an order: 53.4, 54.1, 55.7 and 59.1 (the April and July rates are from the orders themselves, read on DPE's website)
an order read from the site gives its rate, its number and date in words and its PDF; the list agrees, so nothing is said about a difference
an order that is a picture and is in my list: the rate is mine (54.1), the link is the site's
a new order that is a picture and not in my list: no rate (never guessed), the order is named and its link given, and the card is told to open it
a new order with text gives its rate by itself, without anything of mine
when the site's text and my list differ, the site's rate is used and my list's is named so that the card can say it
with no site at all (it could not be read), my list alone answers; a quarter with neither has no order
the rupees of DA on a basic pay at a rate, to the nearest rupee: 50,000 at 59.1% is 29,550; 56,100 at 59.1% is 33,155.1, so 33,155; 56,150 at 59.1% is 33,184.65, so 33,185
